newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS EASIER, EYES TURNING TO FOMC NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS EASIER, EYES TURNING TO FOMC NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Belgian bonds drifted to slightly easier levels in late trading on Wednesday, with the market expected to get increasingly nervous at the approach of next Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's FOMC.

"We've seen good consolidation after the hectic day yesterday. But it's still difficult to see the exact trends for the coming days, with no particular economic data for the rest of the week," one trader said.
He thought it was still possible the benchmark Bund yield could rise to 6.00 percent, which would take OLO yields to 6.10 or 6.15 percent. "At that level it's a buy signal," he added.
One dealer said he expected the benchmark to remain under pressure with the prospect of an auction next Monday where the March 2007 and March 2001 OLOs will be up for sale.
At 1640 GMT the March 2007 OLO was yielding 6.05 percent compared to 6.04 percent at the previous close, its spread over equivalent Bunds narrowing one basis point to 13 bps.
U.S. Treasuries rose early on Wednesday then erased gains after slightly stronger than expected inflation data.
One Belgian dealer said he was expecting a rate hike at the FOMC meeting, but that this appeared to have been priced in by the markets,
